title: Bounds on valid code and clock fields
statement: For a bit string $z$ satisfying the validity guard, the code field and clock field each have length at most the length of $z$.
replaced: For a bit string $z$, write $s(z)$ for its odd split (the self-delimiting pair encoding $\langle z_{[:i]}, z_{[i:]}\rangle$ when $|z| = 2i+1$, and the empty word when $|z|$ is even), $\pi_1, \pi_2$ for the two components of a pair encoding (the empty word when parsing fails), $Y = \pi_1(s(z))$ and $W = \pi_2(s(z))$; the code, input, width and clock fields of $z$ are $\pi_1(Y)$, $\pi_1(\pi_2(Y))$, $\pi_1(\pi_2(\pi_2(Y)))$ and $\pi_2(\pi_2(\pi_2(Y)))$. The guard $G(z)$ holds when $s(z)$, $Y$, $\pi_2(Y)$ and $\pi_2(\pi_2(Y))$ all parse as pair encodings and the width and clock fields consist only of ones. If $G(z)$ holds, then the code field and the clock field of $z$ each have length at most $|z|$.
